speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and arm weakness first started? Did these symptoms appear suddenly or have they been gradually worsening over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as drooping eyelids, or any difficulty with swallowing and speaking? Also, do your symptoms worsen later in the day compared to the morning?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any drooping eyelids, or do you find it difficult to swallow or speak, especially as the day progresses? I also need to confirm if your muscle weakness is symmetrical in both your arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to verify if your eyelids droop, particularly when you look upward or as you get tired later in the day. Could you also confirm if your double vision resolves when you close one eye? REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve Stimulation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.6°C (97.9°F), Blood Pressure 125/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 16 breaths/min. Neurological Examination: Ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) present and worsens with sustained upward gaze; diminished motor strength in upper extremities with normal tone; reflexes and sensation are normal. Blood Tests: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies present (elevated). Electromyography (Repetitive Nerve Stimulation): Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation. Imaging (Chest CT): Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the presence of ptosis, fatigable weakness, elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies, and the decreased muscle response on repetitive nerve stimulation, your symptoms are classic for a specific neuromuscular junction disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.
